title: North Korea Needs China and Russia – But Doesn’t Want Its People Admiring Them
author: Lee Sang-yong
text:
Citizens of North Korea waving at President of Russia Vladimir Putin’s motorcade as it passes by them in Pyongyang during Putin’s state visit to North Korea, June 19, 2024. Only state-sanctioned displays of enthusiasm for Russia are permitted.
Credit: Russian Presidential Press and Information Service
For decades, North Korean authorities have taught ordinary citizens not to harbor illusions about South Korea, the United States, and Japan, on the grounds that admiring the culture and lifestyles of “hostile states” could erode faith in the system. But recent developments inside the country suggest the authorities’ vigilance extends well beyond these so-called hostile states. Even China and Russia – partners with whom North Korea is deepening strategic cooperation – are no exception.North Korea needs Chinese goods and capital, and is expanding military and economic cooperation with Russia. Yet it does not permit ordinary citizens to envy China’s standard of living or Russia’s technological prowess. The state may draw closer to both countries; however, its people are not allowed to hold any “illusions” about them. This contradiction reveals less about North Korea’s foreign policy than about the underlying logic that keeps its system intact.[...]
